name: Dark Yellow Green
lede: Dark Yellow Green is a saturated olive-leaning green, a descriptive survey name with no history of its own.

sections.title: The name
sections.body:
The name comes from the xkcd color survey of 2010, where volunteers typed their own names for screen colors, and no earlier record exists in our sources [1]. Its nearest named neighbors are [[olive]], about 8 units away, and Ugly Green [1]. It is a plain description: a green pulled toward yellow and darkened.

The one place a book puts these words together is a false lead. Gage quotes Newton's 1669 to 1670 Cambridge lectures, which list eleven steps of the spectrum, among them dark yellow and then green as separate steps [2]. Newton later reduced the list to seven [2]. So the books say nothing about this as a color name.

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive only 7 of 23,781 paintings, or 0.03 per cent, hold a color near this swatch, which makes it rarer than 77 per cent of the named colors [3]. Read this as a screen color, not a pigment [3].

questions.q: Where does the name Dark Yellow Green come from in our sources?
True or false: Newton listed dark yellow and green as separate steps in his early lectures.

openers: Newton once counted eleven steps in the spectrum, with dark yellow and green as separate ones, before settling on seven.
